> for the selected Love Burn proposal. Dimensions, depicted equipment, LED
> allocations and delivery status below describe that earlier study; they are

# S25 — 2.5 m sphere, common holder and aerial rig

**Outcome:** G25's holder, with detachable lower legs retained for ground
handling, becomes a suspended study using three over-sphere webbing paths,
collector, swivel and controlled lowering system. The person remains central
to the concept; this plan does not authorize lifting a person.

The generic CAD host is 4.8 m high. The 2.5 m model collector centre is 3.170 m
and its swivel envelope reaches 3.530 m, before actual hoist/pulley and
clearance allowances. Measure usable attachment height, not catalogue peak height.

| Step | Action | Release condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Complete G25 steps 1–5 and select the exact sphere/holder revision. | Occupied stationary sphere and support requirements known. |
| 2 | Andrew identifies the actual aerial rig, manual, configuration, ownership/loan permission and condition. | Exact usable height, attachment/load permissions, outdoor restrictions and inspection history. |
| 3 | Rigger checks the full swept envelope: sphere, side/rear arms, entry, legs/pads, webbing, swivel and lowering path. | No clashes or blocked entry; host compatibility established. |
| 4 | Engineer/rigger defines the complete occupied load path, sling contact and unequal-load cases, joints, payload, hoisting and rescue. Sphere supplier confirms applicable contact/attachment use. | Accepted system design, hardware schedule and operating/weather limits. A generic lyra swivel is insufficient evidence. |
| 5 | Decide whether the selected host is usable at all; compare the host alternatives if not. | Rejected/unknown host means no occupied suspension. Ground mode remains the candidate fallback. |
| 6 | Quote every selected suspension part and the required services, then reconcile cash with the $3,000 total. | Actual commitments for loans/in-kind work; no zero-dollar suspension assumption. |
| 7 | Fabricate the common holder's approved lifting interfaces, retaining the clear-front orientation; inspect completed parts. | Finished mass, inspection records and documented interface compatibility. |
| 8 | Rigger assembles the selected rig on approved footing exactly to its instructions, then fits the specified lifting/retention/lowering system. | Assembly inspection, documented restraint/ballast and secured exclusion area. |
| 9 | Fit the empty sphere and over-sphere webbing with manufacturer-approved contact protection. Install optics before final balance checks. | No seam/entry conflict; all cables, arms, optics and covers included in payload/recovery review. |
| 10 | Perform the reviewer-defined unoccupied tests and controlled recovery rehearsal; prepare a ground receiving/support arrangement. | Test record meets actual criteria; no improvised occupant proof test. |
| 11 | Train and staff the operation, obtain venue acceptance and release the exact configuration for any approved occupied rehearsal. | Rigger/operator roles, stop authority, communications and retrieval demonstrated. |
| 12 | Operate only within that release; lower/close using the approved sequence when conditions require. Strike and inspect all lifting components. | Log each use, damage and return; retire suspect gear from service pending review. |

**BOM:** G25 common holder/sphere + SUSPENSION + selected host + selected optics.
Ground legs may remain in the transport kit but their mass is included in the
lift only if carried. The central front bay remains clear of host feet and
spreader ropes as well as the holder's own hardware.
